intro: Some people receive food, fluids and medicines directly into the stomach through a PEG tube; careful, respectful support keeps them safe and nourished.
points: PEG feeding is a delegated clinical task needing task-specific training, assessed competence and delegation by a nurse or dietitian.
Never restart a feed through a tube you are unsure about or that has been dislodged — stop and escalate.
A dislodged or pulled-out PEG is an emergency; the stoma can close within hours, so get help and never reinsert it.
Keep the person sitting upright at 30 to 45 degrees during and after feeds to reduce aspiration risk.
Give only prescribed feed, flushes and medicines, flushing with prescribed water before and after to prevent blockages.
Watch the stoma and person, reporting infection, leakage, blockage, aspiration signs or dehydration promptly to the nurse.
